chunks: the most beloved of Allah's creatures to Him is a servant whom Allah has empowered against his own self, so he immersed himself in grief and donned fear; the lamp of guidance shone in his heart, and he prepared refreshment for the day that will befall him. He regards the distant as near and the difficult as easy; he looks and perceives, he remembers and increases [in good deeds], and he quenches his thirst from sweet, flowing water whose sources were made easy for him. So he drinks to satisfaction and walks a new path, having cast off the garments of desires and freed himself from worries, except for one worry in which he is unique. He has emerged from the quality of blindness and the company of people of whim, and has become one of the keys to the doors of guidance and the locks on the doors of ruin.

key_terms.مَفَاتِيحُ أَبْوَابِ الْهُدَى: keys to the doors of guidance

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual characteristics of the most beloved servant of Allah according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from the 'Letter to Imam Hasan' (Khutbah al-Hanin context), Imam Ali (AS) describes the ideal believer who achieves spiritual elevation through *zuhd* (asceticism) and *muraqabah* (God-consciousness). By shedding the garments of desire and anxiety, the believer transitions from the state of heedlessness to becoming a key to the gates of guidance, embodying the Shia concept of the *Mu'min al-Kamil* who balances inner tranquility with active preparation for the Hereafter.
